questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a lower triangular matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-5$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=6.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=6.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =6.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -11 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{1}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}-11{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -11 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -11 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{0}{1}=0.$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-(3)(2)) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -10) & =0 \\ -(\lambda -1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda -5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =5.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{12}{5}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ -9 & 7 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ -9 & 7 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 \\ -9 & 4 & 5 \\ -5 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -9{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ -9 & 4 & 5 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{9}{5}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{2}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{2}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{5}(2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2{x}_{3}+3{x}_{3}) \\  & ={x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}:=(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\  & ={x}_{2}+2(0) \\  & ={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 \\ -1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )[(3-\lambda )^{2}-1] & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +8) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -4)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=4,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-(2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{3}{1}=3.$
